title: Canonical pro-etale constant coefficient maps respect composition
statement:
Let $h:Z\to Y$ and $k:Y\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. For $T=X,Y,Z$ use the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $c_f:f^{-1}A_{\mathrm{target}(f)}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathrm{source}(f)}$ be the canonical map preserving constant sections of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and let $\alpha_{h,k}:(k\circ h)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}k^{-1}$ be the inverse-image composition isomorphism compatible with the inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then
$$c_{k\circ h}=c_h\circ h^{-1}(c_k)\circ\alpha_{h,k,A_X}:(k\circ h)^{-1}A_X\longrightarrow A_Z.$$
This is an equality of ring-sheaf maps, including when $Z$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, and Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf: canonical inverse-image composition and constant sections; specialized to ring objects on the small pro-etale sites

proof.text:
Work in sheaves of commutative rings. Write $L_f=f^{-1}$, $R_f=f_*$, and $\eta_f$ for the adjunction unit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], the maps $c_f$ in the item are precisely the maps of that definition, so their adjuncts are its constant-section maps $\rho^f:A_{\mathrm{target}(f)}\to R_fA_{\mathrm{source}(f)}$. For an object $B\to X$, the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the isomorphism
$$\phi_B:Z\times_Y(Y\times_X B)\xrightarrow{\sim}Z\times_X B,$$
with projections to $Z$ and $B$ unchanged. Its inverse is induced by the projection to $Z$ and the pair consisting of $h$ of that projection and the projection to $B$. Both composites preserve the two projections, hence are identities. The same uniqueness proves naturality in $B$. For a ring sheaf $G$ on $Z$, restriction $G(\phi_B)$ therefore defines a natural ring-sheaf isomorphism
$$d_G:R_{kh}G\xrightarrow{\sim}R_kR_hG.$$
Indeed the two evaluations are $G(Z\times_XB)$ and $G(Z\times_Y(Y\times_XB))$ by the direct-image definition; naturality in $G$ is naturality of a sheaf morphism.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (section-morphism), base-change direct-image formula; explicit fibre-product universal-property calculation

proof.text:
The constant coefficient sheaf $A_X$ is the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. We claim
$$d_{A_Z}\circ\rho^{kh}=R_k(\rho^h)\circ\rho^k:A_X\longrightarrow R_kR_hA_Z.$$
Precompose both sides with the constant presheaf's canonical map to $A_X$. At every $B\to X$ and $a\in A$, the left side first gives the constant section $a$ on $Z\times_XB$, then restricts it along $\phi_B$, still giving $a$. The right side first gives $a$ on $Y\times_XB$ and then gives $a$ on $Z\times_Y(Y\times_XB)$, by the defining formula for $\rho$ in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Restrictions preserve these sections because the canonical map from the constant presheaf is natural and that presheaf's restrictions are identities. The two presheaf maps agree; the uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], with target the ring sheaf $R_kR_hA_Z$, proves the claimed equality.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), applied to rings via the cited sheafification definition

proof.text:
Put $L=L_{kh}$, $R=R_{kh}$, $L'=L_hL_k$, and $R'=R_kR_h$. The composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives $L'\dashv R'$ with
$$\eta'_M=R_k(\eta_{h,L_kM})\circ\eta_{k,M}.$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $(L_1,R_1)=(L,R)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(L',R')$ and $\delta=d^{-1}:R'\to R$. It characterizes the comparison $\alpha:L\to L'$ by
$$R(\alpha_M)\circ\eta_{kh,M}=d^{-1}_{L'M}\circ\eta'_M.$$
Equivalently $d_{L'M}R(\alpha_M)\eta_{kh,M}=\eta'_M$. This is the adjunction-compatible comparison specified in the item, with its direction fixed; no other isomorphism of inverse-image functors is substituted. The ring-sheaf adjunctions used here are those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

proof.text: No step assumes any scheme is nonempty. More explicitly, if $Z=\varnothing$, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] says $A_Z$ and $L_{kh}A_X$ are zero ring sheaves and $c_{kh}$ is their unique isomorphism. Both sides of the claimed equality are morphisms between these same zero ring sheaves, hence coincide. This does not assert that distinct elements of $A$ give distinct constant sections.

The math is correct. Step 1: phi_B is a Z-isomorphism with the right variance, giving d=G(phi_B). Step 2: both maps send a to the constant a on the constant presheaf, so uniqueness of sheafification in rings gives the equality. Step 3: the conjugate lemma with delta=d^{-1}:R_kR_h->R_kh gives alpha:L_kh->L_hL_k in the right direction, and the composite unit is R_k(eta_h L_k)eta_k. Step 4: unit naturality at c_k and the triangle identities give R_k(rho^h)rho^k. Step 5: naturality of d, cancelling d and injectivity of the adjunction bijection give the equality. Step 6: the empty case is redundant but correct. Edge cases tested: Z empty, A=0, identity h or k, and a disconnected object. proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle and no cited node is merged. lean.statement:
theorem proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap_comp
    {Z W V : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ W) (k : W ⟶ V)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] :
    proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap (h ≫ k) A =
      (ProEtale.supportSiteProEtaleComparisonComp CommRingCat.{u + 1} h k).hom.app
          (proEtaleConstantRing V A) ≫
        (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
          (proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap k A) ≫
        proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap h A
lean.note: Exact existing theorem of lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition. The coefficient maps are the constant-section adjuncts, identified by prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map; the comparison is the adjunction mate of canonical fibre-product associativity. CommRingCat expresses the commutative-ring-sheaf maps in this statement. No nonempty-scheme hypothesis.
